patch.value:
**Type:** implementation slice of the accepted SDK-first/backend-neutral direction; precise API and adapter design remain proposals. Parent: [#1399](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1399). Prerequisite: typed authoritative ports/inventory. Reuse [#1470](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1470) replay/fault machinery and [#1472](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1472) retained format controls rather than new invariant engines.

**Outcome:** adapter authors implement native storage once; PM behavior remains shared. A new SDK operation composed only of existing ports works unchanged across conforming adapters. SQLite/Postgres/MySQL are separate native adapters/packages, not copies of the CLI or filesystem translators.

**Work and acceptance:**

- Publish a versioned conformance runner accepting an isolated backend factory and declared capabilities. Execute the same public SDK scenarios for create/update/claim/release/delete/restore, schema/custom fields, relationships/tombstones, settings, history and idempotent replay. Start with bounded scenarios then cover the full checked inventory; report unsupported/skipped/incomplete separately from passed.
- Include stable identity across restart, stale-revision CAS, concurrent writers, acknowledged history consistency, unknown-ack reconciliation, hook ordering, malformed/unknown fields, deterministic ordering, complete pagination under relevant consistency mode, and reference resolution. Verify timestamp/number/null/case/collation semantics rather than allowing SQL defaults to change query meaning. Optional query pushdown must match the shared semantic oracle; fallback must remain bounded and honestly costed.
- Preserve the [existing compensating transaction contract](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/df5bf4aa4db17b7743b4f6bfddb32098f2cbd521/src/sdk/workspace-transaction.ts#L29-L94). Test database-native atomic transactions separately from multi-step inspect/apply/compensate recovery; never label an external multi-step workflow atomic merely because one step uses SQL.
- Run filesystem and one minimal native database adapter through the same suite before freezing the port. SQLite is a useful first local proof, not evidence for PostgreSQL/MySQL isolation, lock, durability or driver behavior; each later native engine needs its own bounded integration matrix and receipt. A mock/in-memory pass is not native-engine certification.
- Prove capability refusal before side effects when requested atomicity/history/consistency is unavailable. Inject lost responses, duplicate retry, process interruption and competing revisions; deliberate dropped-audit/stale-write/pagination mutants must fail for the expected reason.
- Add a test-only SDK-composed operation using existing ports and prove adapters require no source changes. Keep adapter contract-version compatibility/discovery explicit; genuine new storage capabilities can require an upgrade, ordinary CLI feature additions should not.
- Document native backend support, limitations and guarantees in one capability matrix. Keep default install lightweight; optional drivers and no mandatory live database connection. No production credentials or paid integrations in tests.

**Limits:** finite conformance does not prove every interleaving. Required native cases unavailable in CI are incomplete/blocking for that claim, not green. Do not duplicate provider-specific schema/auth/rate-limit semantics inside the core; separate adapter-specific contract from shared PM semantics.


**Intake:** Targeted all-status issue searches and canonical source records were rechecked on 2026-10-25. Reuse #1399 / `pm-gh1399` as the parent; if a more specific canonical owner already covers this slice, attach it there rather than create a competing PM item. This report is static source evidence at `df5bf4aa4db17b7743b4f6bfddb32098f2cbd521`, not executed backend tests or a claim of a reproduced defect. No deadline, assignee, deployment or backend switch is implied.

Versioned isolated conformance factory; shared public SDK scenarios, native filesystem and database proof, concurrency/fault negative controls and explicit unsupported or incomplete outcomes.
